subject: English
passage: The Crescent Folios are a set of 64 jazz arrangements credited to the cornetist Marcus Halloway, the pianist Ada Beaumont, and the bandleader Theodore Pace. They were issued anonymously by a small Chicago publisher between 1924 and 1926 and were intended to demonstrate that orchestral techniques could be adapted to the emerging idiom of hot jazz. Although the authorship of most arrangements has been firmly established, that of several remains disputed: for instance, while Folio No. 9, "Riverbend Stomp," was almost certainly arranged by Beaumont, Folio No. 41, "Lakeshore Drag," may have been the work of either Halloway or Pace.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To summarize a contested claim advanced in a collection of arrangements.
choices.B: To describe a collection of arrangements and address what is known about their authorship.
choices.C: To point out that some arrangements in a notable collection were created by one person, while others were created by two people working together.
choices.D: To present the publication history of a collection of arrangements.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The text first describes what the Crescent Folios are: a set of 64 jazz arrangements credited to three musicians, issued in Chicago between 1924 and 1926 to show that orchestral techniques could be adapted to hot jazz. The text then turns to authorship, noting that while most arrangements have firmly established authors, several remain disputed, with one example of certain attribution and one of uncertain attribution. Thus, the main purpose is to describe the collection and address what is known about their authorship.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The text does mention the purpose behind the arrangements (to demonstrate that orchestral techniques could be adapted to hot jazz), but it does not summarize this as a contested claim, nor does it dwell on this point. More importantly, this choice ignores the second half of the text, which addresses questions of authorship.
